bull_bear.body:
- Multi-brand portfolio spanning premium to value segments - Ingersoll Rand, CompAir, Gardner Denver and the newly launched Champion brand
- Long-standing India franchise dating back to 1921, reporting its 104th year
- Part of the Ingersoll Rand Group, giving access to global technology, product platforms and export channels
- New Sanand facility adds advanced technology, testing and localisation capability for air treatment and compression systems
- Breadth of product range from contact-cooled rotary and VSD machines to oil-free and centrifugal frames above 10,000 cfm, enabling differentiated higher-value offerings
- Large and growing installed base underpinning a recurring aftermarket in spares, service, energy audits, rentals and upgrades
- Localisation strategy - 'In India; For India; By India' - supported by supplier localisation and alternate source development
- Digital capability through the Ecoplant compressed-air monitoring and optimisation platform
- Debt-free balance sheet with adequate cash to meet capex as well as developmental and operational requirements
- Service network strength and continued investment in technology innovation and new product launches
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Persistent and interconnected external risk environment — The Company states the external risk environment is increasingly persistent, interconnected and difficult to predict, with geopolitical developments, supply chain volatility and macroeconomic shifts continuing to influence energy and input costs, logistics and freight dynamics, and the availability of critical supplies. This has shortened planning cycles and increased the need for preparedness against low-probability, high-impact events.
- Climate change and energy-use risk — Identified in the BRSR as both risk and opportunity. Climate-related strategic, physical and transitional (market and compliance) risks are becoming steadily more relevant to the business and, if not managed properly, can affect operations and profitability; mitigation is aligned with the parent organization's 2030 and 2050 goals, with site-specific KPIs at the Naroda facility. Negative financial implication cited is increased operating costs in meeting those goals and targets.
- Product innovation and technology obsolescence — The BRSR flags that inability to develop new products and technologies can impair the Company's competitive position, which could affect sales and market share. Mitigation is continued investment in technology innovation, new efficiency models across rotary oil-flooded and oil-free screw compressors, centrifugal upgrades, an expanded heat-of-compression desiccant dryer portfolio and the Ecoplant digital platform.
- Regulatory cost of energy-efficient product design — The BRSR cites higher investments required to meet stringent regulatory requirements on energy-efficient product design as a negative financial implication of the product stewardship and innovation material issue.
- Human rights, labour and talent risk — The BRSR identifies the need to spot human rights risk within operational processes, which could otherwise create reputational or legal risk, alongside the dependence of productivity and operations on employee wellbeing, upskilling and deployment of employee skills.
- Related-party concentration with the group counterparty — Material related-party transactions with Industrial Technologies and Services LLC, USA exceed the SEBI materiality threshold and require shareholder approval, with the resolution placed before the ensuing AGM - a recurring dependence on the parent group that is subject to annual member approval.
- Single business-activity and product concentration — The BRSR reports Air Solutions - manufacturing of air compressors, spare parts and components, installation and commissioning, and air accessories - as 100% of turnover, with manufacture of pumps/compressors/taps and valves at 91% and installation services at 9%, leaving the Company fully exposed to one product-market cycle.
- Export-market exposure — Exports contribute 19% of total turnover per the BRSR, exposing the Company to overseas demand, trade policy and currency conditions in addition to its PAN-India base of 28 states and 8 Union Territories.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company manufactures industrial air compressors and air-treatment equipment and provides comprehensive solutions including installation, commissioning and maintenance. Air Solutions is the only segment in the Company's operations, and its products are primarily sold to industries in the automotive, metals, pharmaceutical and textile sectors. Alongside equipment sales, the growing installed base supports an aftermarket in preventive maintenance, spare parts, energy audits, rentals, upgrades and system optimisation services.

business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Ingersoll Rand Group — related party: The Company states it is part of the Ingersoll Rand Group; the group's ultimate holding company is referenced in the related-party disclosures.
- Industrial Technologies and Services LLC (ITS LLC), USA — related party: Material related-party counterparty for which member approval is sought at the AGM under an omnibus approval. Transactions cover sales of goods and services (exports), purchase of raw materials, components and traded goods, recovery towards business support and auxiliary services (IT services including back-office server maintenance, web page maintenance, IT infrastructure, Cloud IoT, digital engineering, digital transformation, analytics and cyber security, recovered at cost plus a minimum mark-up of 15%), and administrative services availed (strategy and continuous improvement, finance and treasury, IT deployment, taxation and regulatory matters) allocated at actual cost with no mark-up. The Company depends substantially on ITS LLC for its export sales and consequently for its revenue generation; products are manufactured at the Company's Naroda/Sanand, Ahmedabad factory and services are rendered primarily from the Bengaluru office. Contracts/work orders are valid for 1-2 years and the proposed tenure is for financial year 2026-27.
- Gardner Denver Ltd., United Kingdom — related party: A wholly owned subsidiary of the ultimate holding company. Mr. Gareth Topping, Director of the Company, is an employee of this entity and may be deemed concerned or interested; apart from him, no Director or KMP is interested in the related-party transactions.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Advance the innovation roadmap around oil-free low-pressure solutions for the power and infrastructure sectors while scaling contact-cooled rotary technologies for the rapidly expanding Tier-2 industrial market
- Ramp the new Sanand, Gujarat facility as the platform for launching new and localized air treatment and compression system applications
- Local innovation and market creation on an 'In India; For India; By India' basis
- Supplier localisation, alternate source development and inventory planning to reduce single-source dependency and supply-chain exposure
- Supply-chain diversification and strategic sourcing to manage geopolitical, logistics and freight disruption
- Move up the mix into premium, differentiated technologies - VSD compressors, permanent magnet motors, heat recovery systems and oil-free compressed air
- Digitalisation of the offering through IoT-enabled smart compressors, predictive maintenance, remote monitoring and energy analytics, anchored on the Ecoplant platform
- Expand the aftermarket around the growing installed base - preventive maintenance, spare parts, energy audits, rentals, upgrades and system optimisation
- Strengthen the service network and field service capability
- Grow exports from India as a regional manufacturing hub into Asia, Middle East and Africa
- Disciplined pricing actions, productivity improvements and cost optimisation to protect margins against inflation and commodity volatility
- The stated objective of the Company's dividend distribution policy is to reward shareholders by sharing a portion of the profits while ensuring sufficient funds are retained in the Company for growth, working capital requirements and capex requirements. The policy aims to provide a regular dividend income to shareholders alongside long-term capital appreciation, and the Company seeks to strike an optimum balance between the quantum of dividend paid and the profits retained in the business. Factors considered in the payout decision include contractual obligations, taxation policy, statutory covenants, historical financial performance, future financial outlook, current-year profits and outlook, operating cash flows, possibilities of alternate usage of cash, and provision for unforeseen events and contingencies. The Board may modify or amend the policy depending on business needs and the external environment. There were no loans and advances in the nature of loans to firms or companies in which directors were interested.
- Parent organization has set 2030 and 2050 goals focused on reducing greenhouse gas emissions and energy use, creating safer water for communities and reduced waste to landfill; the Naroda manufacturing facility has established site-specific key performance targets in line with those parent goals and targets.
- Limited assurance on BRSR Core for FY2025-26 obtained from TÜV Rheinland (India) Private Limited as the appointed Assurance Provider, per SEBI Listing Regulations.
- Product stewardship agenda covering implementation of environmental aspects in manufacturing, development and adoption of a Product Stewardship Policy, and the ability to reduce Scope 3 emissions.
- Energy-efficient product development: best-efficiency models introduced in the 15-22 kW rotary oil-flooded and 90-160 kW oil-free screw compressor segments, continued focus on variable frequency drive models across all Tier products for optimum part-load efficiency, and an upgraded CC700 plant-air centrifugal model.
- Localisation of heated blower desiccant dryer models and an enhanced heat-of-compression desiccant dryer portfolio with higher flow ranges.
- Ecoplant smart compressed air management tool introduced to Indian customers, using cloud data monitoring and machine learning algorithms for dynamic control of compressors to deliver energy savings.
- Board gender diversity: women represent 33.33% of the Board of Directors; the Company reports its gender-wise workforce composition and states nil transgender employees.
- Risk Management Committee constituted under Regulation 21 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, comprising Board members and senior executives, to frame, implement and monitor the risk management plan, with the Audit Committee holding additional oversight of financial risks and controls; all properties and insurable interests are fully insured.
- Directors and Officers (D&O) insurance obtained for all Directors and members of Senior Management per Regulation 25(10).
- POSH: zero-tolerance policy with an Internal Compliance Committee; nil sexual harassment complaints received and nil pending during the year, with one awareness workshop conducted and POSH training mandatory for all employees.
- Full compliance with the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, including paid maternity leave, nursing breaks, protection from dismissal during maternity leave and no discrimination in recruitment or service conditions.
- Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for communities, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners, including an external ethics reporting channel.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed sections contain no named capex project, capacity addition or commissioning timeline for the Company. Expansion is described only in general terms: the Company states that its ongoing investments in localization, digitalization, energy-efficient technologies and aftermarket expansion are expected to strengthen long-term growth and improve operational leverage, and that it continues to address competitive and geopolitical challenges through localization initiatives, supply chain diversification, innovation, digital capabilities and strengthening of its service network. On the demand side it points to expansion opportunities in the aftermarket around its growing installed base (preventive maintenance, spare parts, energy audits, rentals, upgrades and system optimisation) and to expanding exports to Asia, Middle East and Africa as India emerges as a regional manufacturing hub. The wider industry context cited is India's capital goods structural shift during 2025, driven by government infrastructure outlays, accelerating private capital expenditure and the Make in India initiative, with growth into emerging segments such as EV infrastructure and data centers.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Growth in industrial activity, infrastructure investments, electronics manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, food processing, automotive and emerging sectors such as data centers has supported demand for compressed air solutions and aftermarket services
- The Indian air compressor market is expected to continue growing at a healthy pace driven by structural demand factors
- India's continued industrialization supported by Make in India, Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes, semiconductor manufacturing investments, electronics production growth, infrastructure development and automotive/EV expansion is expected to drive sustained demand
- Increasing customer focus on energy efficiency, sustainability and operating cost reduction is accelerating adoption of premium technologies such as VSD compressors, permanent magnet motors, heat recovery systems and oil-free solutions - a mix and value-per-unit lever
- Pharmaceuticals, food & beverage, electronics, healthcare and semiconductor manufacturing are increasingly adopting oil-free technologies for contamination control, providing opportunity for differentiated higher-value offerings
- Digitalisation creates new growth avenues through IoT-enabled smart compressors, predictive maintenance, remote monitoring, energy analytics and lifecycle management
- The growing installed base provides a substantial aftermarket opportunity - a recurring revenue and margin cushion
- Ongoing investments in localization, digitalization, energy-efficient technologies and aftermarket expansion are expected to strengthen long-term growth and improve operational leverage
- Margin management is being run through strategic sourcing, localization, productivity improvements and disciplined pricing against inflationary pressure, commodity volatility, logistics cost increases and foreign exchange fluctuations
- India's real GDP is projected by the IMF to grow 6.5% in FY 2026-27 and 6.5% in FY 2027-28; the World Bank projects 6.6% growth in FY 2026-27 as higher energy prices and supply chain disruption weigh on activity - a macro demand backdrop, not company guidance
- Headwind: global economic uncertainties, evolving trade policies, geopolitical tensions and inflationary pressures may delay customer capital expenditure decisions and impact demand visibility
- Headwind: price pressure in the value segment from low-cost imports from China and Southeast Asia, spurious products and non-compliant compressor packages affecting market discipline and margins
- No company order book or pipeline figure is disclosed. The only order-book reference is industry-level: order books for large heavy engineering and machinery firms surged to Rs. 5.2 lakh crore by late 2025, sustaining double-digit revenue growth and expansion into emerging segments like EV infrastructure and data centers.

summary.oneLiner: Ingersoll-Rand (India) Limited is a leading manufacturer of industrial air compressors in India, selling and servicing compressed-air systems under the Ingersoll Rand, CompAir, Gardner Denver and Champion brands with a presence dating back to 1921.
summary.business: The Company manufactures industrial air compressors and air-treatment equipment and provides comprehensive solutions including installation, commissioning and maintenance. Air Solutions is the only segment in the Company's operations, and its products are primarily sold to industries in the automotive, metals, pharmaceutical and textile sectors. Alongside equipment sales, the growing installed base supports an aftermarket in preventive maintenance, spare parts, energy audits, rentals, upgrades and system optimisation services.

risks.risk: Persistent and interconnected external risk environment
risks.note: The Company states the external risk environment is increasingly persistent, interconnected and difficult to predict, with geopolitical developments, supply chain volatility and macroeconomic shifts continuing to influence energy and input costs, logistics and freight dynamics, and the availability of critical supplies. This has shortened planning cycles and increased the need for preparedness against low-probability, high-impact events.

Identified in the BRSR as both risk and opportunity. Climate-related strategic, physical and transitional (market and compliance) risks are becoming steadily more relevant to the business and, if not managed properly, can affect operations and profitability; mitigation is aligned with the parent organization's 2030 and 2050 goals, with site-specific KPIs at the Naroda facility. Negative financial implication cited is increased operating costs in meeting those goals and targets.

The BRSR flags that inability to develop new products and technologies can impair the Company's competitive position, which could affect sales and market share. Mitigation is continued investment in technology innovation, new efficiency models across rotary oil-flooded and oil-free screw compressors, centrifugal upgrades, an expanded heat-of-compression desiccant dryer portfolio and the Ecoplant digital platform.

risks.risk: Regulatory cost of energy-efficient product design
risks.note: The BRSR cites higher investments required to meet stringent regulatory requirements on energy-efficient product design as a negative financial implication of the product stewardship and innovation material issue.

risks.risk: Human rights, labour and talent risk
risks.note: The BRSR identifies the need to spot human rights risk within operational processes, which could otherwise create reputational or legal risk, alongside the dependence of productivity and operations on employee wellbeing, upskilling and deployment of employee skills.

risks.risk: Related-party concentration with the group counterparty
risks.note: Material related-party transactions with Industrial Technologies and Services LLC, USA exceed the SEBI materiality threshold and require shareholder approval, with the resolution placed before the ensuing AGM - a recurring dependence on the parent group that is subject to annual member approval.

The BRSR reports Air Solutions - manufacturing of air compressors, spare parts and components, installation and commissioning, and air accessories - as 100% of turnover, with manufacture of pumps/compressors/taps and valves at 91% and installation services at 9%, leaving the Company fully exposed to one product-market cycle.

Exports contribute 19% of total turnover per the BRSR, exposing the Company to overseas demand, trade policy and currency conditions in addition to its PAN-India base of 28 states and 8 Union Territories.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Growth in industrial activity, infrastructure investments, electronics manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, food processing, automotive and emerging sectors such as data centers has supported demand for compressed air solutions and aftermarket services
- The Indian air compressor market is expected to continue growing at a healthy pace driven by structural demand factors
- India's continued industrialization supported by Make in India, Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes, semiconductor manufacturing investments, electronics production growth, infrastructure development and automotive/EV expansion is expected to drive sustained demand
- Increasing customer focus on energy efficiency, sustainability and operating cost reduction is accelerating adoption of premium technologies such as VSD compressors, permanent magnet motors, heat recovery systems and oil-free solutions - a mix and value-per-unit lever
- Pharmaceuticals, food & beverage, electronics, healthcare and semiconductor manufacturing are increasingly adopting oil-free technologies for contamination control, providing opportunity for differentiated higher-value offerings
- Digitalisation creates new growth avenues through IoT-enabled smart compressors, predictive maintenance, remote monitoring, energy analytics and lifecycle management
- The growing installed base provides a substantial aftermarket opportunity - a recurring revenue and margin cushion
- Ongoing investments in localization, digitalization, energy-efficient technologies and aftermarket expansion are expected to strengthen long-term growth and improve operational leverage
- Margin management is being run through strategic sourcing, localization, productivity improvements and disciplined pricing against inflationary pressure, commodity volatility, logistics cost increases and foreign exchange fluctuations
- India's real GDP is projected by the IMF to grow 6.5% in FY 2026-27 and 6.5% in FY 2027-28; the World Bank projects 6.6% growth in FY 2026-27 as higher energy prices and supply chain disruption weigh on activity - a macro demand backdrop, not company guidance
- Headwind: global economic uncertainties, evolving trade policies, geopolitical tensions and inflationary pressures may delay customer capital expenditure decisions and impact demand visibility
- Headwind: price pressure in the value segment from low-cost imports from China and Southeast Asia, spurious products and non-compliant compressor packages affecting market discipline and margins
- No company order book or pipeline figure is disclosed. The only order-book reference is industry-level: order books for large heavy engineering and machinery firms surged to Rs. 5.2 lakh crore by late 2025, sustaining double-digit revenue growth and expansion into emerging segments like EV infrastructure and data centers.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Advance the innovation roadmap around oil-free low-pressure solutions for the power and infrastructure sectors while scaling contact-cooled rotary technologies for the rapidly expanding Tier-2 industrial market
- Ramp the new Sanand, Gujarat facility as the platform for launching new and localized air treatment and compression system applications
- Local innovation and market creation on an 'In India; For India; By India' basis
- Supplier localisation, alternate source development and inventory planning to reduce single-source dependency and supply-chain exposure
- Supply-chain diversification and strategic sourcing to manage geopolitical, logistics and freight disruption
- Move up the mix into premium, differentiated technologies - VSD compressors, permanent magnet motors, heat recovery systems and oil-free compressed air
- Digitalisation of the offering through IoT-enabled smart compressors, predictive maintenance, remote monitoring and energy analytics, anchored on the Ecoplant platform
- Expand the aftermarket around the growing installed base - preventive maintenance, spare parts, energy audits, rentals, upgrades and system optimisation
- Strengthen the service network and field service capability
- Grow exports from India as a regional manufacturing hub into Asia, Middle East and Africa
- Disciplined pricing actions, productivity improvements and cost optimisation to protect margins against inflation and commodity volatility
- The stated objective of the Company's dividend distribution policy is to reward shareholders by sharing a portion of the profits while ensuring sufficient funds are retained in the Company for growth, working capital requirements and capex requirements. The policy aims to provide a regular dividend income to shareholders alongside long-term capital appreciation, and the Company seeks to strike an optimum balance between the quantum of dividend paid and the profits retained in the business. Factors considered in the payout decision include contractual obligations, taxation policy, statutory covenants, historical financial performance, future financial outlook, current-year profits and outlook, operating cash flows, possibilities of alternate usage of cash, and provision for unforeseen events and contingencies. The Board may modify or amend the policy depending on business needs and the external environment. There were no loans and advances in the nature of loans to firms or companies in which directors were interested.
- Parent organization has set 2030 and 2050 goals focused on reducing greenhouse gas emissions and energy use, creating safer water for communities and reduced waste to landfill; the Naroda manufacturing facility has established site-specific key performance targets in line with those parent goals and targets.
- Limited assurance on BRSR Core for FY2025-26 obtained from TÜV Rheinland (India) Private Limited as the appointed Assurance Provider, per SEBI Listing Regulations.
- Product stewardship agenda covering implementation of environmental aspects in manufacturing, development and adoption of a Product Stewardship Policy, and the ability to reduce Scope 3 emissions.
- Energy-efficient product development: best-efficiency models introduced in the 15-22 kW rotary oil-flooded and 90-160 kW oil-free screw compressor segments, continued focus on variable frequency drive models across all Tier products for optimum part-load efficiency, and an upgraded CC700 plant-air centrifugal model.
- Localisation of heated blower desiccant dryer models and an enhanced heat-of-compression desiccant dryer portfolio with higher flow ranges.
- Ecoplant smart compressed air management tool introduced to Indian customers, using cloud data monitoring and machine learning algorithms for dynamic control of compressors to deliver energy savings.
- Board gender diversity: women represent 33.33% of the Board of Directors; the Company reports its gender-wise workforce composition and states nil transgender employees.
- Risk Management Committee constituted under Regulation 21 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, comprising Board members and senior executives, to frame, implement and monitor the risk management plan, with the Audit Committee holding additional oversight of financial risks and controls; all properties and insurable interests are fully insured.
- Directors and Officers (D&O) insurance obtained for all Directors and members of Senior Management per Regulation 25(10).
- POSH: zero-tolerance policy with an Internal Compliance Committee; nil sexual harassment complaints received and nil pending during the year, with one awareness workshop conducted and POSH training mandatory for all employees.
- Full compliance with the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, including paid maternity leave, nursing breaks, protection from dismissal during maternity leave and no discrimination in recruitment or service conditions.
- Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for communities, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners, including an external ethics reporting channel.

JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.
themes.driver: Capacity expansion going live (JYOTICNC); defence/EMS order conversion; US-reshoring export demand (ELGIEQUIP).

hero.oneLiner: Ingersoll-Rand (India) Limited is a leading manufacturer of industrial air compressors in India, selling and servicing compressed-air systems under the Ingersoll Rand, CompAir, Gardner Denver and Champion brands with a presence dating back to 1921.
